content.text: Reviewing a large PR (81 files, ~6.7k lines). Reading the core new scripts now.

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: implement
commands.description: Execute sprint tasks with production-quality code and tests (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: review-sprint
commands.description: Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.name: autocompact
commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.name: color
commands.description: Set the prompt bar color for this session

commands.name: compact
commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.name: output-style
commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.name: context
commands.description: Show current context usage

commands.name: effort
commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.description: Toggle fast mode (Opus 5.5)

commands.description: Toggle focus view: just your prompt, summary, and response

commands.name: heapdump
commands.description: Dump the JS heap to the Desktop; on Linux with no Desktop folder, the home directory

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Manage MCP servers

commands.name: model
commands.description: Set the AI model for Claude Code

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec
commands.description: Execute a server-launched workflow handoff (workflow_launch event sessions only)

commands.name: reload-plugins
commands.description: Activate pending plugin changes in the current session

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Show session cost, plan usage, and what's contributing to your limits

commands.name: insights
commands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

commands.name: recap
commands.description: Generate a one-line session recap now

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

commands.name: list-agents
commands.description: List subagents, teammates, and other Claude sessions you can message

commands.name: team-onboarding
commands.description: Help teammates ramp on Claude Code with a guide from your usage

#!/usr/bin/env bash # ============================================================================= # guard-yield.sh — the guard register and its 30-day host yield (cycle-129 FR-1) # ============================================================================= # Enumerates every guard Loa ships and joins it with its origin and its yield: # hooks every command registered in .claude/settings.json, parsed against # the canonical schema "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"/.claude/ [args] # (or the same wrapped in hook-guard.sh); one row per unique script # fences the `# @guard fence:` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, # cross-checked both ways against its emit_block call sites and # its literal `pattern_id: ""` audit constants # validators the `# @guard validator:` markers in validate-artifact.sh # gates the fixed list in the origin map (each row's `script` must exist) # policies the floor policies in the origin map # Origins, class, status, knob and floor come from .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml; # the floor set must equal .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards. # # Outputs: # grimoires/loa/guards.md tracked, STRUCTURAL ONLY (a pure function of the # repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it # .run/guard-yield.md, .json untracked host yield: blocks_30d, likely_fp_30d, # telemetry_30d, last_real_catch per guard # hooks-reference.md table with --hooks-table, the rows between # and # # Yield (SDD D-1.3): rows of .run/audit.jsonl and its rotated segments # .run/audit.jsonl.* with action == "block", plus implement-gate rows (telemetry # when action is telemetry or ask), with ts inside the window. Replays are # excluded and counted: replay == true (LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 at the source), or, # for rows that predate the flag, a cwd under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ or containing # /bats-run-, /bats., /evals/results/ or /sandbox/, or a UTC minute holding # BURST_ROWS (10) or more block rows (a suite replaying fixtures into the live # log from inside the repository; no interactive session blocks ten commands in # one minute). A block is a likely false # positive (a heuristic) when its command holds a heredoc (`<<`; or, when # .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh defines heredoc_nonexec, a heredoc # that function calls non-executing), when its cwd lies outside the repository # (this checkout and its main worktree), or when its pattern id is a prose class # (SP-1, FR-MERGE-2, FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) with no destructive verb at statement start. # A real catch is a block that is not a likely false positive. # # Privacy: no command text, cwd, hostname, user or model name is written to any # output; ids match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$; origin text comes from the tracked map. # # Usage: # guard-yield.sh [--window-days 30] [--audit-log PATH] [--origins PATH] # [--floor PATH] [--out grimoires/loa/guards.md] [--yield-dir .run] # [--hooks-table] [--check] [--json] [--root DIR] # [--settings PATH] [--fence PATH] [--validator PATH] # [--hooks-ref PATH] [--now YYYY-MM-DD|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ|EPOCH] # # Exit codes: # 0 written, or in sync (--check) # 1 drift (--check): guards.md or the hooks table differ from what would be written # 2 usage error # 3 unreadable or unparseable input (a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield) # 5 a guard without an origin row, a row that resolves to nothing, an invalid row, # a floor mismatch, or a hook command outside the canonical schema # # Tested by tests/unit/guard-yield.bats and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats. # ============================================================================= set -euo pipefail export LC_ALL=C SCRIPT_NAME="guard-yield.sh" SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)" usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Tested/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//' -e '/^Tested/d' } die() { local code="$1"; shift; echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: $*" >&2; exit "$code"; } warn() { echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: WARN: $*" >&2; } ROOT="" WINDOW_DAYS=30 AUDIT_LOG="" ORIGINS="" FLOOR="" OUT="" YIELD_DIR="" HOOKS_REF="" SETTINGS="" FENCE="" VALIDATOR="" NOW="" DO_HOOKS_TABLE=0 DO_CHECK=0 DO_JSON=0 need_arg() { [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die 2 "$1 needs a value (see --help)"; } while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in --window-days) need_arg "$@"; WINDOW_DAYS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --audit-log) need_arg "$@"; AUDIT_LOG="$2"; shift 2 ;; --origins) need_arg "$@"; ORIGINS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --floor) need_arg "$@"; FLOOR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --out) need_arg "$@"; OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;; --yield-dir) need_arg "$@"; YIELD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --root) need_arg "$@"; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;; --settings) need_arg "$@"; SETTINGS="$2"; shift 2 ;; --fence) need_arg "$@"; FENCE="$2"; shift 2 ;; --validator) need_arg "$@"; VALIDATOR="$2"; shift 2 ;; --hooks-ref) need_arg "$@"; HOOKS_REF="$2"; shift 2 ;; --now) need_arg "$@"; NOW="$2"; shift 2 ;; --hooks-table) DO_HOOKS_TABLE=1; shift ;; --check) DO_CHECK=1; shift ;; --json) DO_JSON=1; shift ;; -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; *) die 2 "unknown argument '$1' (see --help)" ;; esac done [[ "$WINDOW_DAYS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$WINDOW_DAYS" -ge 1 && "$WINDOW_DAYS" -le 3650 ]] \ || die 2 "--window-days must be an integer from 1 to 3650 (got '$WINDOW_DAYS')" command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "jq is required" command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "yq v4 (mikefarah) is required" case "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" in *mikefarah*"version v4."*) ;; *) die 3 "yq v4 (mikefarah) is required; found: $(yq --version 2>&1 | head -1)" ;; esac if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.."; fi [[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die 3 "--root '$ROOT' is not a directory" ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)" : "${ORIGINS:=$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml}" : "${FLOOR:=$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml}" : "${OUT:=$ROOT/grimoires/loa/guards.md}" : "${YIELD_DIR:=$ROOT/.run}" : "${SETTINGS:=$ROOT/.claude/settings.json}" : "${FENCE:=$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh}" : "${VALIDATOR:=$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh}" : "${HOOKS_REF:=$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md}" : "${AUDIT_LOG:=$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl}" HEREDOC_LIB="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh" BURST_ROWS=10 REGEN_HINT="regenerate: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table" # The time base: --now, else the clock. Day granularity is all any output shows. if [[ -z "$NOW" ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(date -u +%s)" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$NOW" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(jq -rn --arg d "${NOW}T00:00:00Z" '$d | fromdateiso8601')" || die 2 "--now '$NOW' is not a date" elif [[ "$NOW" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$ ]]; then NOW_EPOCH="$(jq -rn --arg d "$NOW" '$d | fromdateiso8601')" || die 2 "--now '$NOW' is not a timestamp" else die 2 "--now takes YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or epoch seconds (got '$NOW')" fi TMPWORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guard-yield.XXXXXX")" cleanup() { rm -rf -- "$TMPWORK"; } trap cleanup EXIT # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- inputs for f in "$ORIGINS" "$FLOOR" "$SETTINGS" "$FENCE" "$VALIDATOR"; do [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || die 3 "input not readable: $f" done MAP_JSON="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ORIGINS" 2>/dev/null)" || die 3 "origin map does not parse as YAML: $ORIGINS" [[ -n "$MAP_JSON" && "$MAP_JSON" != "null" ]] || die 3 "origin map is empty: $ORIGINS" FLOOR_JSON="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$FLOOR" 2>/dev/null)" || die 3 "floor file does not parse as YAML: $FLOOR" jq -e 'type == "object"' "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 3 "settings file does not parse as a JSON object: $SETTINGS" ERRORS="$TMPWORK/errors" : > "$ERRORS" # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- map schema jq -r ' def idok: type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$"); def nonempty: type == "string" and length > 0; (if .schema_version != 1 then "origin map: schema_version must be 1" else empty end), (if (.guards | type) != "array" then "origin map: guards must be a list" else ((.guards | map(.id) | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1) | .[0]))[] | "origin map: duplicate id \(tostring)"), (.guards[] | . as $r | ($r.id | tostring) as $id | (if ($r.id | idok | not) then "origin map: row id \($id) does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$" else empty end), (if (($r.kind // "") | IN("hook","fence","validator","gate","policy") | not) then "\($id): kind must be hook|fence|validator|gate|policy" else empty end), (if ($id | startswith(($r.kind // "?") + ":") | not) then "\($id): the id prefix must equal its kind" else empty end), (if (($r.class // "") | IN("harness","script","prose") | not) then "\($id): class must be harness|script|prose" else empty end), (if (($r.status // "") | IN("active","dormant","telemetry") | not) then "\($id): status must be active|dormant|telemetry" else empty end), (if ($r.origin.ref | nonempty | not) then "guard \($id) has no origin (origin.ref is empty)" else empty end), (if (($r.origin.kind // "") | IN("kf","issue","finding","cycle","design") | not) then "\($id): origin.kind must be kf|issue|finding|cycle|design" else empty end), (if ($r.knob | nonempty | not) then "\($id): knob must be a config key, an env var or none" else empty end), (if ($r.floor | type) != "boolean" then "\($id): floor must be true or false" else empty end), (if (($r.registrations // []) | type != "array" or any(.[]; type != "string")) then "\($id): registrations must be a list of strings" else empty end), (if $r.status == "dormant" and (($r.knob // "") | test("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$") | not) then "\($id): a dormant row names the arming env var in knob" else empty end), (if ($r.kind == "gate" or $r.kind == "policy") and ($r.script | nonempty | not) then "\($id): gate and policy rows name their script" else empty end), (if ($r.note // "" | type) != "string" then "\($id): note must be a string" else empty end) ) end) ' <<<"$MAP_JSON" >> "$ERRORS" || die 3 "origin map could not be checked: $ORIGINS" if [[ -s "$ERRORS" ]]; then sed "s/^/$SCRIPT_NAME: /" "$ERRORS" >&2 exit 5 fi # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- hooks # jq parses each registered command against the canonical schema; bash resolves # symlinks once and checks the script exists. US (0x1f) separates fields so an # empty matcher survives `read`. US=$'\x1f' HOOK_LINES="$TMPWORK/hooks.lines" jq -r ' def pfx: "\"\\$\\(git rev-parse --show-toplevel\\)\"/\\.claude/"; def path_re: "(?

[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+)"; def args_re: "(?( [A-Za-z0-9._=-]+)*)"; def badpath: split("/") | any(.[]; . == "" or . == "." or . == ".."); (.hooks // {}) | to_entries[] | .key as $e | (.value // [])[] | (.matcher // "") as $m | (.hooks // [])[] | (.command // "") as $c | ( ([$c | capture("^" + pfx + "hooks/hook-guard\\.sh " + pfx + path_re + args_re + "$")?] | .[0]) as $w | if $w != null then (if ($w.p | badpath) then ["bad", $c] else ["ok", $e, $m, $w.p, "1"] end) else (([$c | capture("^" + pfx + path_re + args_re + "$")?] | .[0]) as $d | if $d != null and ($d.p != "hooks/hook-guard.sh") and ($d.p | badpath | not) then ["ok", $e, $m, $d.p, "0"] else ["bad", $c] end) end ) | if any(.[]; explode | any(.[]; . < 32 or . == 127)) then ["bad", "(a command with control characters)"] else . end | join("\u001f") ' "$SETTINGS" > "$HOOK_LINES" || die 3 "settings hooks could not be enumerated: $SETTINGS" HOOK_ROWS="$TMPWORK/hooks.jsonl" : > "$HOOK_ROWS" while IFS="$US" read -r tag ev mt rel wrapped; do [[ -n "$tag" ]] || continue if [[ "$tag" != "ok" ]]; then echo "hook command outside the canonical schema \"\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)\"/.claude/ [args] (or wrapped in hook-guard.sh): $ev" >> "$ERRORS" continue fi abs="$ROOT/.claude/$rel" if [[ -L "$abs" ]]; then tgt="$(readlink "$abs")" case "$tgt" in /*) ;; *) tgt="$(dirname "$abs")/$tgt" ;; esac tdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$tgt")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || tdir="" canon="$tdir/$(basename "$tgt")" case "$canon" in "$ROOT/.claude/"*) rel="${canon#"$ROOT/.claude/"}"; abs="$canon" ;; *) echo "hook script .claude/$rel is a symlink that leaves .claude/ (registered for $ev)" >> "$ERRORS"; continue ;; esac fi if [[ ! -f "$abs" ]]; then echo "hook script .claude/$rel registered for $ev does not exist" >> "$ERRORS" continue fi case "$rel" in hooks/*) id="hook:${rel#hooks/}" ;; *) id="hook:$rel" ;; esac if [[ -n "$mt" ]]; then reg="$ev:$mt"; else reg="$ev"; fi jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg rel "$rel" --arg ev "$ev" --arg mt "$mt" --arg reg "$reg" --arg w "$wrapped" \ '{id: $id, rel: $rel, event: $ev, matcher: $mt, registration: $reg, wrapped: ($w == "1")}' >> "$HOOK_ROWS" done < "$HOOK_LINES" HOOKS_JSON="$(jq -cs '.' "$HOOK_ROWS")" # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- fence markers # Sites: `emit_block ""` calls and literal `pattern_id: ""` audit constants on # non-comment lines. Each site needs a marker with its id within the 8 lines above; # each marker needs a site with its id within the 8 lines below. FENCE_IDS="$TMPWORK/fence.ids" awk -v errs="$ERRORS" ' function note(s) { print s >> errs } /^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*@guard[[:space:]]+fence:/ { s = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*@guard[[:space:]]+fence:/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s) if (s !~ /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/) { note("fence marker at line " NR " has an invalid id"); next } nm++; mline[nm] = NR; mid[nm] = s; next } /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next } { line = $0 if (line ~ /emit_block[[:space:]]*\(\)/) next while (match(line, /emit_block[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+/)) { tok = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH); line = substr(line, RSTART + RLENGTH) sub(/^emit_block[[:space:]]+/, "", tok) if (tok ~ /^"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"$/) { gsub(/"/, "", tok); ns++; sline[ns] = NR; sid[ns] = tok } else note("fence emit_block call at line " NR " has a non-literal pattern id; give it a literal id and a # 1	# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
     2	#
     3	# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
     4	# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
     5	#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the

    10	# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is

# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
#
# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
#
# Row fields:
#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)
#   knob           the config key or env var that arms, relaxes or disables it, or none
#   floor          true exactly for the ids in .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards
#   registrations  hook rows: every "<Event>:<matcher>" (or "<Event>" when the
#                  registration has no matcher) from .claude/settings.json; [] otherwise
#   script         gate and policy rows: the file that implements it (must exist)
#   note           one line; the hooks-reference table's Purpose column for hook rows
schema_version: 1
guards:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v0.19.0 b10450fa"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Skill(plan-and-analyze.*)"]
    note: "Archive the previous cycle's discovery context before /plan-and-analyze"
  - id: hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-011"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Bash"]
    note: "Block destructive commands and System-Zone shell writes (the fence; per-pattern rows are fence:<id>)"
  - id: hook:safety/team-role-guard.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: dormant
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-020 (#337)"}
    knob: LOA_TEAM_MEMBER
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Bash"]
    note: "Enforce lead-only operations in Agent Teams (armed only when LOA_TEAM_MEMBER is set)"
  - id: hook:safety/team-role-guard-write.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: dormant
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-020 (#337)"}
    knob: LOA_TEAM_MEMBER
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "Block teammate writes to the System Zone, state files and append-only files (armed only when LOA_TEAM_MEMBER is set)"
  - id: hook:safety/spiral-dispatch-guard.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-072"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "Block inline implementation writes under /spiraling until spiral-harness.sh is dispatched"
  - id: hook:safety/zone-write-guard.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-106"}
    knob: LOA_ZONE_GUARD_DISABLE
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "Block project-work writes into the framework zone (bounded marker .run/zone-guard-authorization.json for framework development)"
  - id: hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-050 FR-7"}
    knob: implement_gate.mode
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "ADVISORY: ask on an App Zone write outside an active implementation run, on a write to the gate's own trust inputs, and when the write cannot be evaluated; never blocks"
  - id: hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-124 FR-10"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "Refuse a write that would grow grimoires/loa/NOTES.md at or over 200 KiB (shrinking edits and notes-guard.sh rotate pass)"
  - id: hook:safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: issue, ref: "#552"}
    knob: flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"]
    note: "Block a COMPLETED marker write when cross-model dissent is enabled and its artefact is missing or invalid (the floor row is gate:adversarial-review-gate)"
  - id: hook:safety/team-skill-guard.sh
    kind: hook
    class: harness
    status: dormant
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-020 (#337)"}
    knob: LOA_TEAM_MEMBER
    floor: false
    registrations: ["PreToolUse:Skill"]
    note: "Block lead-only skill invocations for teammates (armed only when LOA_TEAM_MEMBER is set)"
  - id: hook:safety/spiral-skill-sentinel.sh
    kind: hook
    class: script
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-128 D-6.4"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: []
    note: "validate-artifact.sh --type glossary: entry length, aliases and fences"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- gates (fixed list, SDD D-1.1)
  - id: gate:verdict-derive
    kind: gate
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-119"}
    knob: none
    floor: true
    registrations: []
    script: .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
    note: "LOA-VERDICT trailer and prose agree; the review and audit verdict consumers read it"
  - id: gate:adversarial-review-gate
    kind: gate
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: issue, ref: "#552"}
    knob: flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
    floor: true
    registrations: []
    script: .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
    note: "COMPLETED is refused without the cross-model dissent artefact when dissent is enabled"
  - id: gate:implement-gate
    kind: gate
    class: harness
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-050 FR-7"}
    knob: implement_gate.mode
    floor: false
    registrations: []
    script: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh
    note: "App Zone writes outside an implementation run ask; never blocks today"
  - id: gate:success-criteria
    kind: gate
    class: prose
    status: active
    origin: {kind: issue, ref: "#961"}
    knob: karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria
    floor: false
    registrations: []
    script: .claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md
    note: "/implement checks the sprint plan for a non-empty success-criteria section before starting"
  - id: gate:dissent-budget
    kind: gate
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: issue, ref: "#224"}
    knob: flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_cents
    floor: false
    registrations: []
    script: .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh
    note: "the dissent spend cap; a malformed cap fails closed at 0 cents"
  - id: gate:seams
    kind: gate
    class: script

# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
_drop_md_section() {
  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
  awk -v h="$heading" '
    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
    skip { n++; next }
    { print }
    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
  mv "$tmp" "$f"
  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
}

# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
_drop_paragraph() {
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
import re, sys
path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
            removed = paras[i]
            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
            del paras[i:i + 2]
            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
            sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PY
}

apply_toggles() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"

          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
        fi
        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi

        ;;
      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")
  return 0
}

refusal_fallbacks="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="system" and .subtype=="model_refusal_fallback")
  | {from: (.original_model // null), to: (.fallback_model // null), category: (.api_refusal_category // null),

  --arg model_requested "$MODEL" \
  --arg effort "$effort" \
  --arg prompt_tree "$PROMPT_TREE" \
  --arg prompt_tree_sha "$prompt_tree_sha" \
  --arg prompt_tree_commit "$prompt_tree_commit" \
  --argjson prompt_tree_dirty "$prompt_tree_dirty" \
  --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
  --arg trial_id "$TRIAL_ID" \
  --argjson rc "$rc" \
  --argjson is_error "$is_error" \
  --argjson duration_ms "$duration_ms" \

  --argjson tool_writes "$tool_writes" \

  --arg source_commit "${LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT:-$prompt_tree_commit}" \
  --argjson refusal_fallbacks "$refusal_fallbacks" \

    output_tokens: (u.output_tokens // u.outputTokens // 0),

     else $model_requested end) as $model_id |

    model_id: $model_id,

    usage: norm_usage($result.usage // {}),
    models_used: ($mu | with_entries(.value = (.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0))),
    refusal_fallbacks: $refusal_fallbacks,
    tool_writes: $tool_writes,
    arm: $arm,
    arm_toggles: $arm_toggles,

     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)

     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch

    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless

    44	#

   301	    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \

   305	set_state() { STATE="$1"; write_status; }
   306	
   307	# --- one trial (runs in a background job; writes its row to $JOBS_DIR/<id>.row)
   308	is_transport_failure() {  # is_transport_failure <sandbox-ws>
   309	  local ws="$1" out="$1/.eval/agent-output.json" err="$1/.eval/agent-stderr.log" rc
   310	  rc="$(jq -r '.exit_code // 0' "$ws/.eval/executor.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   311	  case "$rc" in 124|137|143) return 0 ;; esac
   312	  [[ "$(jq -r '.subtype // ""' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" == "missing" ]] && return 0
   313	  [[ -n "$(jq -r '.api_error_status // empty' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" ]] && return 0
   314	  grep -qiE 'rate.?limit|overloaded|session limit|usage limit|out of extra usage|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|network|socket hang up|5[0-9][0-9] ' \
   315	    "$err" "$out" 2>/dev/null && return 0

   319	run_trial() {  # run_trial <job-id> <arm> <fixture> <trial>
   320	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" fx="$3" trial="$4"
   321	  local task="$EVALS_DIR/tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$fx.yaml" task_id="$TASK_PREFIX-$fx"
   322	  local run_id="arms-$SUITE-$BATCH" attempt=0 ws="" trial_id status="error" err_json='null'
   323	  local graders='[]' composite='{"strategy":"all_must_pass","pass":false,"score":0}' executor='null'
   324	  local start_ms end_ms per_trial ex_rc
   325	  per_trial="$(yq -r '.timeout.per_trial // 1500' "$task")"
   326	  start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   327	  if ! verify_corpus "$fx" >"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.digest" 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift"; then
   328	    printf 'DRIFT\n' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag"; return 0
   329	  fi
   330	  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
   331	    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
   332	    trial_id="$run_id-$arm-$fx-t$trial-a$attempt-$jid"
   333	    ws="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" create --fixture "review-prs/$fx" --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" 2>/dev/null)" \
   334	      || { err_json='{"type":"infrastructure_error","message":"sandbox creation failed"}'; break; }
   335	    ex_rc=0
   336	    EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$WORKTREE" EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL" LOA_EVAL_ARM="$arm" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$SUITE_FILE" \
   337	      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT="$SRC_FULL" LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
   338	      "$SCRIPT_DIR/execute-agent.sh" --task-yaml "$task" --workspace "$ws" \
   339	        --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" --timeout "$per_trial" \
   340	        >/dev/null 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log" || ex_rc=$?
   341	    [[ -f "$ws/.eval/executor.json" ]] && executor="$(cat "$ws/.eval/executor.json")"
   342	    if [[ $ex_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
   343	      local gout gexit=0
   344	      gout="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/grade.sh" --task-yaml "$task" --workspace "$ws" \
   345	        --timeout "$(yq -r '.timeout.per_grader // 60' "$task")" 2>/dev/null)" || gexit=$?
   346	      if jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$gout"; then
   347	        graders="$(jq -c '.graders' <<<"$gout")"; composite="$(jq -c '.composite' <<<"$gout")"
   348	      fi
   349	      if [[ $gexit -le 1 ]]; then status="completed"; err_json='null'
   350	      else err_json='{"type":"infrastructure_error","message":"grader error"}'; fi
   351	      break
   352	    fi
   353	    if [[ $ex_rc -eq 1 ]] && is_transport_failure "$ws"; then
   354	      err_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$attempt" '{type:"transport_error",message:"executor transport failure",attempt:$a}')"
   355	      if [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then

   358	        ws=""; executor='null'
   359	        sleep "$RETRY_WAIT"; continue
   360	      fi
   361	    else
   362	      err_json="$(jq -cn --argjson rc "$ex_rc" '{type:(if $rc == 2 then "infrastructure_error" else "agent_error" end),message:("execute-agent exit " + ($rc|tostring))}')"
   363	    fi
   364	    break
   365	  done
   366	  end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   367	  if [[ -n "$ws" && -d "$ws" ]]; then
   368	    keep_artifacts "$ws" "$arm" "$task_id" "$trial" ""
   369	    "$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" destroy --trial-id "$trial_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   370	  fi
   371	  jq -cn --arg run_id "$run_id" --arg batch "$BATCH" --arg suite "$SUITE" --arg task_id "$task_id" \

   373	    --arg status "$status" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --arg run_date "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" \
   374	    --argjson duration_ms "$(( end_ms - start_ms ))" --arg src "$SRC_FULL" --arg model_req "$MODEL" \
   375	    --argjson executor "$executor" --argjson graders "$graders" --argjson composite "$composite" \
   376	    --argjson error "$err_json" --arg digest "$CORPUS_DIGEST" --arg digest_now "$(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.digest" 2>/dev/null)" \
   377	    '{schema_version: 1, run_id: $run_id, batch: $batch, suite: $suite, task_id: $task_id, fixture: $fixture,
   378	      arm: $arm, trial: $trial, attempts: $attempts, status: $status, timestamp: $ts, run_date: $run_date,
   379	      duration_ms: $duration_ms, source_commit: $src, model_requested: $model_req,

   381	      corpus_sha256: $digest, corpus_sha256_at_trial: $digest_now, fixture_verified: true, graders: $graders, composite: $composite, error: $error}
   382	     + (if $executor == null then {} else {executor: $executor} end)' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp"
   383	  mv "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"
   384	}

   386	keep_artifacts() {  # keep_artifacts <ws> <arm> <task_id> <trial> <suffix>
   387	  local ws="$1" dest="$BATCH_DIR/$2/artifacts/$3/trial-$4$5" f
   388	  mkdir -p "$dest"

   391	  done

   393	  # the raw transcript only on request (it embeds every tool result)
   394	  [[ "${EVAL_KEEP_EVENTS:-0}" == "1" && -f "$ws/.eval/events.jsonl" ]] && cp "$ws/.eval/events.jsonl" "$dest/events.jsonl"
   395	  return 0
   396	}
   397	
   398	# Parent-side: append a finished job's row and update the counters.
   399	collect() {  # collect <job-id> <arm>
   400	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" i
   401	  i="$(arm_index "$arm")"
   402	  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag" ]]; then
   403	    log "corpus drift before $jid: $(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift" 2>/dev/null)"
   404	    set_state failed; exit 3
   405	  fi
   406	  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
   407	    mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
   408	    cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" >> "$BATCH_DIR/$arm/results.jsonl"
   409	    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
   410	      DONE[$i]=$(( ${DONE[$i]} + 1 ))
   411	      log "done $jid ($(jq -r '"\(.arm) \(.fixture) t\(.trial) recall=\(([.graders[]? | select(.name=="recall-vs-defects.sh") | .details.recall][0]) // "n/a") \(.duration_ms/1000|floor)s"' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   412	    else
   413	      FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   414	      log "FAILED $jid ($(jq -c '.error' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   415	    fi
   416	    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
   417	  else
   418	    FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   419	    log "FAILED $jid (no row written; see $JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log)"
   420	  fi
   421	  write_status
   422	}
   423	
   424	log "start suite=$SUITE batch=$BATCH source=$SRC12 model=$MODEL trials=${#PLAN[@]} concurrency=$CONCURRENCY worktree=$WORKTREE"
   425	write_status
   426	trap 'log "interrupted"; set_state failed; exit 3' INT TERM HUP
   427	
   428	PIDS=() PJOB=() PARM=()
   429	reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
   430	  local i
   431	  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
   432	    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
   433	      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
   434	        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
   435	        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PARM[$i]}"
   436	        unset 'PIDS[i]' 'PJOB[i]' 'PARM[i]'
   437	        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PARM=("${PARM[@]+"${PARM[@]}"}")
   438	        break
   439	      fi
   440	    done
   441	    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep 1
   442	  done
   443	  return 0
   444	}
   445	
   446	n=0
   447	for p in "${PLAN[@]}"; do
   448	  IFS='|' read -r a f t <<<"$p"
   449	  n=$((n + 1)); jid="$(printf 'j%04d' "$n")"
   450	  reap "$CONCURRENCY"
   451	  run_trial "$jid" "$a" "$f" "$t" &
   452	  PIDS+=("$!"); PJOB+=("$jid"); PARM+=("$a")
   453	done
   454	reap 1
   455	
   456	total_done=0 total_failed=0
   457	for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do total_done=$(( total_done + ${DONE[$i]} )); total_failed=$(( total_failed + ${FAILED[$i]} )); done
   458	if [[ $total_failed -eq 0 ]]; then
   459	  set_state complete; log "complete: $total_done trials"; exit 0
   460	elif [[ $total_done -eq 0 ]]; then
   461	  set_state failed; log "failed: no trial completed ($total_failed failed)"; exit 3
   462	else
   463	  set_state partial; log "partial: $total_done done, $total_failed failed"; exit 1
   464	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

   134	verify_corpus() {

   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")

    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))

   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)

   135	            self.cells[fx].append((int(row.get("trial") or 0), float(d["recall"])))

     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the

     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
4	# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
5	# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
9	#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
10	#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
11	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
12	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
13	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
14	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
15	#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
16	#
17	# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
18	# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
19	#
20	# Writes (seed):
21	#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
22	#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
23	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
24	#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
25	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
26	#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
27	#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
28	#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
29	#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
30	#
31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
32	# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
33	# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
34	#
35	# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
36	# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
37	# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
38	# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
39	# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
40	# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
41	# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
42	# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
43	# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
44	# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
45	# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
46	# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
47	#
48	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
49	# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
50	# =============================================================================
51	set -euo pipefail
52	export LC_ALL=C
53	
54	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
56	
57	exec python3 -I - "$REPO_ROOT" "$@" <<'PY'
58	import argparse, csv, hashlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

67	ap.add_argument("--feedback"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

69	ap.add_argument("--by"); ap.add_argument("--freeze", action="store_true"); ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
70	ap.add_argument("--repo", default=HARNESS_ROOT)

107	    s = CTRL.sub(" ", s)

113	    r"glpat-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}", r"xox[bpors]-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+", r"sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}",

121	    become a fixed marker, identically in base/, head/ and head.diff; line
122	    numbers never move. Counted in the dropped report."""
123	    if b is None:
124	        return None
125	    t = b.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(b, bytes) else b
126	    for r in SECRET_RX:
127	        t, n = r.subn("REDACTED-TEST-SECRET", t)
128	        REDACTED[0] += n if count else 0
129	    return t.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(b, bytes) else t

139	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS":

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# validate-artifact.sh --type sprint: every task line ends with exactly one
     3	# 'kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' token, gated on the plan's header **Date:**
     4	# (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.1; KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-14; DEC-0144, DEC-0154).
     5	
     6	setup() {
     7	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
     8	    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
     9	    T="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}"
    10	}
    11	
    12	# One sprint block; $1 = the Technical Tasks lines (printf-ready, one per line).
    13	sprint_body() {
    14	    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
    15	    printf '### Technical Tasks\n%s\n\n' "$1"
    16	    printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n| `tool.sh` exit code | a wrong exit | prose | new |\n\n'
    17	    printf '### Dependencies\n- none\n\n### Security Considerations\n- none\n\n'
    18	    printf '### Risks & Mitigation\n| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| r | Low | Low | m |\n\n'
    19	    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'
    20	}
    21	# $1 = header date (may be empty); $2 = sprint 1 task lines; $3 = the E2E task line.
    22	plan() {
    23	    printf '# Sprint Plan: x\n\n**Version:** 1.0\n'
    24	    [[ -n "$1" ]] && printf '**Date:** %s\n' "$1"
    25	    printf '**Author:** test\n\n---\n\n'
    26	    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2"
    27	    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'
    28	    sprint_body '- [ ] Task 2.1: wire the thing → **[G-1]** ⇐ Task 1.1 · kind: mechanical'
    29	    printf '### Task 2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation\n%s\n\n' "$3"
    30	    printf '**Acceptance Criteria:**\n- [ ] Each goal validated with documented evidence\n\n'
    31	    printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
    32	}
    33	TAGGED='- [ ] Task 1.1: add the tool → **[G-1]** ⇐ none · kind: mechanical'
    34	E2E='- [ ] Task 2.E2E: validate every goal → **[G-1]** ⇐ Task 2.1 · kind: judgment'
    35	
    36	@test "KINDS-1 a plan dated 2026-10-14 with an untagged task fails and names the line" {
    37	    plan 2026-10-14 '- [ ] Task 1.1: add the tool → **[G-1]** ⇐ none' "$E2E" > "$T/sprint.md"
    38	    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
    39	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    40	    [[ "$output" == *"sprint.md:"*": a task line has no kind: token"*"on or after 2026-10-14"* ]]
    41	    [ "$(grep -c 'kind: token' <<< "$output")" -eq 1 ]
    42	}
    43	
    44	@test "KINDS-2 the same plan with every task tagged passes without a kind message" {
    45	    plan 2026-10-14 "$TAGGED" "$E2E" > "$T/sprint.md"
    46	    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
    47	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    48	    [[ "$output" != *"kind:"* ]]
    49	}
    50

@@ -22,6 +22,65 @@ ab:
   floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
   corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS
 
+  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
+  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
+  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
+  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
+  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
+  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
+  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
+  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
+  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
+  #                can never license removing the control
+  arms:
+    - id: baseline
+      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
+      toggles: {}
+    - id: no_companion
+      description: >-
+        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
+        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
+        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
+      informational: true
+      toggles:
+        companion_voice: false
+    - id: no_karpathy
+      description: >-
+        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
+        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
+        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
+        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
+      toggles:
+        karpathy_block: false
+    - id: no_rule_files
+      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
+      toggles:
+        rule_files: false
+
+  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
+  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
+  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
+  threshold:
+    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
+    trials_required: 3
+    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
+    coverage_required: full
+    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
+    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
+    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
+    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
+    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
+    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
+    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
+    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
+    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
+    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
+    bootstrap:
+      method: percentile
+      level: 0.90
+      resample: fixtures
+      iterations: 2000
+
 ci:
   gate_type: advisory
   min_trials: 3

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash

     3	# build-review-corpus.sh — build the 10-PR review-recall corpus from this
     4	# repository's own history (cycle-124 Sprint 3, PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6)
     5	#
     6	# Every planted defect is a real shipped fix, inverted: for a `defect` row the
     7	# PR under review turns the FIXED code (base/) back into the BUGGY code
     8	# (head/ = the fix commit's parent), so each defect has a real failing test in
     9	# history and a reviewer must reason about the code, not read a changelog.
    10	# Comment-only lines the fix ADDED (the "why this was wrong" prose) are removed
    11	# from base/ before diffing, so the inverted diff removes code, never a
    12	# confession. `clean` rows are forward fix commits (base = parent, head = fix,
    13	# tests included): a PR with nothing planted, so false positives are measurable.
    14	#
    15	# Inputs (committed):
    16	#   review-prs/corpus.tsv   fixture  kind  commit  file  defect_id  severity  category  must_match
    17	#   review-prs/prs.tsv      fixture  title  description
    18	# Outputs (committed, frozen by SHA256SUMS):
    19	#   review-prs/pr-NN/{PR.md,head.diff,base/…,head/…,fixture.yaml,
    20	#                     REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md}
    21	#   review-prs/manifests/pr-NN.json   HIDDEN — never copied into a sandbox
    22	#   review-prs/SHA256SUMS             the freeze; compare.sh pins its hash
    23	#
    24	# `must_match` is a literal substring that must occur on exactly ONE line of
    25	# the head/ file: that line is the defect's anchor (the grader accepts ±3).
    26	#
    27	# cycle-129: corpus.tsv also carries `record` rows (pr-11 … pr-18, sprints
    28	# 247–254) and `#` gap comments; those fixtures are built by
    29	# evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh (labels in the hidden labels/ dir)
    30	# and skipped here. The freeze below still covers every file in the corpus.
    31	# A rebuild here regenerates pr-01 … pr-10 from scratch; their hand-added
    32	# anchors[] (pr-02 D06, pr-05 D13) are not in corpus.tsv and must be re-added.
    33	#
    34	# Usage:
    35	#   build-review-corpus.sh            # (re)build everything + SHA256SUMS
    36	#   build-review-corpus.sh --verify   # sha256sum -c against the committed freeze
    37	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 verify failed / spec error, 2 usage
    38	# =============================================================================

    40	export LC_ALL=C

    42	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    57	import csv, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys

    60	def git(*args, text=True):

    69	COMMENT = {

    71	    ".yaml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".yml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"),
    72	    ".ts": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"), ".js": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"),

   111	- `base/` — every touched file before the change
   112	- `head/` — every touched file after the change

   171	        hp = os.path.join(fdir, "head", path)

   176	            parts.append(f"diff --git a/{path} b/{path}\n" + p.stdout)

   179	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "PR.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(f"# {meta['title']}\n\n{meta['description']}\n")

   181	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(AUDIT_INSTR)

    95	# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma

Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle

content.content:
log "[LOAD] Found ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks for skill: $SKILL"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "$SUITE" ]]; then
    local suite_file="$SUITES_DIR/${SUITE}.yaml"
    if [[ ! -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Suite not found: $suite_file" >&2
      exit 3
    fi

    # Read include patterns from suite
    local include_count
    include_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.include | length // 0' "$suite_file")"

    for i in $(seq 0 $((include_count - 1))); do
      local pattern
      pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.include[$i]" "$suite_file")"

      # Resolve glob pattern relative to evals/
      # Use bash globbing with globstar for ** patterns
      local had_globstar=false
      shopt -q globstar 2>/dev/null && had_globstar=true
      shopt -s globstar 2>/dev/null || true

      local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi
    done

    # Apply exclude patterns
    local exclude_count
    exclude_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.exclude | length // 0' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
    if [[ "$exclude_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
      local filtered_tasks=()
      for task_file in "${TASK_FILES[@]}"; do
        local excluded=false
        for j in $(seq 0 $((exclude_count - 1))); do
          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break
          fi
        done
        [[ "$excluded" == "false" ]] && filtered_tasks+=("$task_file")
      done
      TASK_FILES=("${filtered_tasks[@]}")
    fi

    # Read suite defaults
    SUITE_TRIALS="$(yq -r '.defaults.trials // 1' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_trial // 120' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_GRADER="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_grader // 30' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_STRATEGY="$(yq -r '.defaults.composite_strategy // "all_must_pass"' "$suite_file")"

    log "[LOAD] Suite '$SUITE': ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks, ${SUITE_TRIALS} trial(s)"
    return
  fi

  # Default: run all tasks
  while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
    TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
  done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | sort | tr '\n' '\0')
  SUITE="all"
  log "[LOAD] Loaded ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks (all)"
}

# Suite defaults
SUITE_TRIALS=1
SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL=120

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats — cycle-124 FR-8 / AC-8.1
#
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh enforces the byte budgets of the always-loaded
# prompt surface: SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read
# resources), CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 10,240 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn
# above 114,688 B). Passes at exactly the limit, fails one byte over.
# PB-10 pins the workflow's header comment to the tool's constants.
# PB-9 is the live gate: red until the Sprint 3 audit lands.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    TOOL="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-prompt-budget.sh"
    T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pb.XXXXXX")"
    mkdir -p "$T/.claude/skills/s1/resources" "$T/.claude/loa" "$T/.claude/protocols"
    P="$T/.claude/protocols"
    fill "$T/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" 100
    fill "$P/a.md" 100
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

fill() {  # fill <path> <bytes> — exactly <bytes> bytes of text
    head -c "$2" /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x' > "$1"
}

@test "PB-1 a SKILL.md of exactly 16,384 bytes passes" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 16384
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T" --quiet
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "PB-2 a SKILL.md of 16,385 bytes fails and the breach names the skill and the byte count" {
    fill "$T/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md" 16385
    run "$TOOL" --root "$T"
    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"skill s1: 16385 B > 16384 B"* ]]

    12	
    13	# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
    14	frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
    15	globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
    16	tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }

    12	# Git Stash Safety
    13	
    14	`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.
    15	
    16	**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.
    17	
    18	## The safe interface
    19	
    20	```bash
    21	source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
    22	stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
    23	```
    24	
    25	Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
    29	git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
    30	(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
    31	git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
    32	```
    33	
    34	## Judgment rules the fence cannot express
    35	
    36	- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
    37	- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.
    38	
    39	## Origin
    40	
    41	- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
    42	- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).
    43	
    44	## Related rules

    46	- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.

     8	# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
     9	# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
    10	# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
    11	# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    18	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    19	  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
    21	  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
    22	  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
    23	  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
    24	  export TMPDIR="$T"
    25	  cp "$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml" "$T/origins.yaml"
    26	  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"

    30	      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
    31	  }
    32	  {
    33	    # live, inside the repo

    35	    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP

    39	    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
    40	    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
    41	    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
    42	    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
    43	      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"

    49	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:05:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", cwd: "x"}'

 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.

+
